identity.wikipedia: Free and Independent State of Cundinamarca

land.text: the Province of Bogotá around the capital, 'the former capital of the Viceroyalty of New Granada'

predecessors.note: The province of Bogotá of the Viceroyalty of New Granada (slug viceroyalty-of-new-granada in the New Granada dossier), which formed its junta in 1810; the page says the state 'included parts of the former New Kingdom of Granada'.

land.text: Cundinamarca, brought into the Union by Bolívar's army in December 1814 (page), and the plains the 1815 shape adds

successors.note: Cliopatria's New Granada 1815 shape adds Cundinamarca; the page has Bolívar force terms on Bogotá in December 1814 and the state then annexed by the United Provinces of New Granada

capitals.name: Santa Fe de Bogotá
capitals.note: The page names Bogotá as the capital, 'the former capital of the Viceroyalty of New Granada'.

rulers.name: Antonio Nariño
rulers.title: President, dictator for life from June 1813
rulers.note: 20 September 1811 - 10 May 1814; acting presidents Luis de Ayala y Vergara (25 June - 5 August 1812), Manuel Benito de Castro Arcaya (19 August - 12 September 1812), Felipe de Vergara Azcárate y Caycedo (26 November - 14 December 1812) and Manuel de Bernardo Álvarez (acting from 13 August 1813).

correction.text: the 1814 outline, held 1811-1813 as well: the Province of Bogotá with its colonial extent

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria draws the state only in 1814 although the page dates it from 1811 ('Established: 1811'; Lozano president from 24 March 1811; the Free and Independent State declared the following month). New Granada's own 1811-1813 shapes leave Cundinamarca out (13 percent of Cundinamarca department only), so the 1814 outline is used for 1811-1813 as well. The page gives no territorial detail beyond 'parts of the former New Kingdom of Granada'.

223,335 km2: Bogotá, 87 percent of Cundinamarca department, 57 percent of Tolima, 55 percent of Caldas and about 660 cells (90 percent of the area) of the eastern plains of Meta and Vichada, which no page opened names. The page gives neither an area nor a list of provinces; the outline stands as the Province of Bogotá in its colonial extent, and the plains are nominal. Nariño's Popayán conquest (January 1814) and the defeat at Pasto (May 1814) are not in the shape; the ledger carries them. The state ends in December 1814 when the United Provinces annex it.

region.text: the Province of Bogotá around the capital, 'the former capital of the Viceroyalty of New Granada'

ledger.note: March 1811: Cundinamarca sets up its government. The page has the province convene a constituent college in March 1811 and a constitution 'the following month' declare the Free and Independent State of Cundinamarca, with Jorge Tadeo Lozano as first president (term from 24 March 1811); infobox 'Established: 1811'. The page names the capital but no boundary.

region.text: Tunja, where the federalist Congress settled

ledger.note: 26 November 1812: Nariño marches on Tunja. The page has him leave to conquer Tunja on 26 November 1812; he was defeated at Ventaquemada on 2 December 1812 and the federalists defeated him again at San Victorino on 9 January 1813. The war with the Congress of the Provinces is the one New Granada's dossier dates from 1812.
July 1813: Cundinamarca declares independence from the Monarchy. 'Cundinamarca finally declared independence from the Monarchy' in July 1813 (no day); Nariño was named dictator for life in June 1813.

region.text: Popayán and Pasto, the royalist south

ledger.note: January 1814: Nariño's army takes Popayán. The page has Popayán captured in January 1814 in the southern campaign and Nariño defeated at Pasto in May 1814, arrested and sent to Cádiz via Quito. It does not say who held Popayán after May.
May 1814: Nariño is defeated at Pasto, arrested and sent to Cádiz via Quito, ending the southern campaign.

region.text: the Province of Bogotá around the capital, 'the former capital of the Viceroyalty of New Granada'

ledger.note: December 1814: Bolívar forces Cundinamarca to terms. The page has Bolívar force terms on Bogotá in December 1814 and the state then annexed by the United Provinces of New Granada. The last president's term ends on 12 December 1814. (The infobox of the page also reads 'Bolivar takes Santafé: 1816', which conflicts with the body.)

region.text: the whole state, including the eastern plains the shape draws

ledger.note: December 1814: Cundinamarca is annexed by the United Provinces (page: the state was then annexed by the United Provinces of New Granada). Cliopatria's New Granada 1815 shape takes in Cundinamarca.
December 1814: the Free and Independent State of Cundinamarca ends in the Union of the United Provinces of New Granada. The page has Morillo's campaign end with the capture of Santafé on 6 May 1816.

wars.name: Civil war between Cundinamarca and the United Provinces of New Granada

zones.text: Tunja and the road from Bogotá

wars.outcome: Nariño lost at Ventaquemada (2 December 1812) and the federalists lost at San Victorino (9 January 1813); in December 1814 Bolívar forced Bogotá to terms and the state was annexed.
wars.note: The page does not give the name of the war.

wars.name: Nariño's southern campaign
wars.outcome: Popayán captured in January 1814; Nariño defeated at Pasto in May 1814, arrested and sent to Cádiz.
wars.note: The page gives no start for the campaign; 1813 is the year of the dictatorship (June).

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes the State's limits; the page gives 'parts of the former New Kingdom of Granada'. The eastern plains are nominal.

notes: Cliopatria's Wikipedia field 'Cundinamarca' is a disambiguation page; the state's article is 'Free and Independent State of Cundinamarca', used here. The page's dates: established 1811 (March), independence declared July 1813, annexed December 1814 (its infobox adds a stray 'Bolivar takes Santafé: 1816'; the body dates Bolívar to December 1814 and Morillo's capture of Santafé to 6 May 1816). Cliopatria has the shape only for 1814; a new keyframe covers 1811-1813. The page names no territory beyond 'parts of the former New Kingdom of Granada', gives no area, and the shape's eastern plains (Meta, Vichada, 90 percent of its area) are not on any page opened. New Granada's dossier (am-08-a) pairs the civil war and the December 1814 union from the other side.
